gaps.description: Claims the closing/reflection stage can run 'any time,' even with pending changes. It requires ALL changes to have status DONE in progress.json before running.
gaps.corpus_ref: MISCONCEPTION: /kbd-reflect can run before all changes are DONE

gaps.description: Reproduces the known misconception that the closing stage is a mid-phase status snapshot tool usable with pending changes.
gaps.corpus_ref: MISCONCEPTION: /kbd-reflect can run before all changes are DONE

gaps.description: Missing coverage of what the closing stage actually produces: a reflection document, per-goal MET/PARTIAL/NOT MET status, technical debt/lessons, recommended next phase, and the sycophancy-correction reflector gate.

transfer_problems: A phase has 5 changes in progress.json: 3 marked DONE and 2 marked IN_PROGRESS. The operator runs the closing/reflection stage anyway. What happens, and why does the corpus say this produces a misleading outcome?

Using the lifecycle sequence new-phase -> assess -> (analyze) -> plan -> execute -> reflect -> (evolve), explain what precondition must hold in progress.json before the reflect stage gate will allow it to run.
